warmup: FULL BODY WARM-UP (Updated for Strength + AMRAP Days)
Step 1: General Warm-Up (Pick 1 activity for 5 minutes)

5-min fast-paced walk or incline treadmill
5-min easy/moderate bike or assault bike
5-min stair climber (light pace)
5-min row (smooth pulls, steady pace)
✅ Goal: Get warm, feel alert, still able to hold a conversation.
Step 2: Full Body Activation Circuit (1–2 Rounds)
Now we’re waking up every major joint + muscle. Keep it fluid, controlled, and intentional.

10 Light DB Lateral Raises
10 Light DB Front Raises
10 Air Squats
10 Controlled Push-Ups (knees or elevated if needed)
10 Arm Circles (forward + backward)
10 Toe Touches (slow hamstring stretch)
10 Torso Rotations (gentle standing twists)
✅ Goal: Loosen up, increase range of motion, start feeling “switched on.”
Step 3: Specific Warm-Up Sets (Before Your First Main Lift)

You should never go straight into your working weight cold. Do 1–3 warm-up sets before your first heavy lift (e.g., squat, bench, row) Use 30–60% of your working weight Increase slowly while focusing on perfect form and full ROM
✅ Goal: Prime your nervous system for output. Movement should feel clean and confident.
⏱️ Total Time: ~10–12 minutes

days.note:
Since this current cycle is 5 days per week, I do not recommend doing any additional work on your rest days. We really need these days to recover so we can keep progressing in those strength numbers each week. Extra activity is only going to hurt your progress, trust me!

Things you can do if you like:
- Go on a walk
- Do a fun activity like biking, surfing, a light jog, etc... Just nothing at maximal efforts!
- Yoga or some kind of mobility/stretching routine

Since nutrition is a big part of our fitness goals, today can also be a great day food shop, meal prep, and remind yourself to dial in this section of your training!

cycles.intro:
FULL BODY AESTHETICS — WEEK 1

👉 New here? Start today. Every 4 weeks we kick off a brand-new training cycle, so you won't miss out by joining now. Complete today's workout, track your progress, and before you know it you'll be right in sync with the CHALK community.

This cycle is a little different—and I think you're going to love it.

Instead of 5 lifting days, we're moving to 4 full-body lifting workouts each week, giving you more recovery while still training every muscle multiple times. We've also added 2 optional conditioning days, so you can improve your fitness without taking away from your strength or muscle-building progress.

Here's what to expect over the next 8 weeks:

• 4 Full-Body Lifting Workouts
• 2 Optional Conditioning Days
• Progressive overload every week
• Brand-new exercise variations in Week 5
• A density finisher after every lifting session

Show up, track your lifts, and focus on getting a little better every week. Eight weeks from now, you'll be stronger, more athletic, and more muscular than when you started.

days.title: Conditioning
days.text:
🔥 Today's conditioning piece is called: "VO2 Max: The Norwegian"

Choose one:
• Rower
• Assault Bike
• Ski Erg
• Run

Complete:
• 4 minutes at 90–95% of your max heart rate
• 3 minutes of very easy recovery
• Repeat for 5 total rounds

This is one of the most proven VO2 max protocols ever developed and is used by elite endurance athletes around the world. The goal is to spend time working at your absolute highest sustainable aerobic capacity to improve your engine.

During each 4-minute effort, you should only be able to get out one or two words at a time. If you can comfortably hold a conversation, back off the talking and turn up the intensity.

Every interval should feel challenging, but your recovery should leave you ready to attack the next round with the same effort. Today is all about building a bigger engine. 🚀

SCORE: You can realistically only score your assault bike, ski erg, or rower here, but if you decide to run, no problem. Today is not as much about the score as it is about the work.

days.text:
⚡ Today's conditioning piece is called: Fifteen Fifteen Sprint

Choose either the rower, assault bike, or ski erg.

Complete:

8-minute warm-up (just easy cruising speed of cardio of your choice)

Then;

12 Rounds: 15 seconds HARD x 15 seconds easy

Rest 4 minutes after the last round.

Repeat everything ONE MORE TIME!

*The goal of this workout is to improve your VO2 max by spending as much time as possible at a very high aerobic intensity. The short recovery keeps your heart rate elevated, allowing you to recover just enough to attack the next sprint.

*Every 15-second effort should be fast and explosive (RPE 9–10/10). During the recovery, keep moving but slow down just enough to prepare for the next sprint. Your goal is to maintain your speed and power from the first sprint all the way to the last. 🚀

SCORE: Total calories combined from all 24 rounds.

days.note:

days.title: SHARK ATTACK
days.text:
Choose ONE: Assault Bike, C2 Rower, Ski Erg, or Run.

Warm‑Up (8 minutes) 

- 6 minutes easy → moderate  
- 4 × 10 seconds fast / 20 seconds easy  

Today's Workout (32 minutes total)

Most of the workout is performed at RPE 6–7, but every 4 minutes the shark attacks and you...

- Sprint 20 seconds all out  
- Immediately return to your RPE 6–7 pace  

Each subsequent attack is longer:

1. 20 seconds  
2. 30 seconds  
3. 40 seconds  
4. 50 seconds  
5. 60 seconds  
6. 70 seconds  
7. 80 seconds  
8. Finish all out  

*Goal: Survive all eight attacks without letting your normal pace fall apart.

*Score: Total calories

*The whole workout in 1 sentence: Maintain a steady RPE 6–7 pace for 32 minutes, sprinting every 4 minutes with each sprint getting 10 seconds longer.

cycles.label: On the Minute cycle, Ladder closers
cycles.intro:
💪 FULL BODY AESTHETICS — ON THE MINUTE CYCLE

👉 NEW HERE? Start with today's workout. This is where everyone starts — a brand new 4-week block kicks off every month, so you haven't missed a thing.

How this block works:

1️⃣ Start with your main lift. Work up to one heavy set (each movement's notes tell you exactly how). Rest as much as you need between sets.

2️⃣ Then it's one exercise per body part — chest, back, legs, shoulders, biceps, triceps. For each one: start a set at the top of every minute for 3-4 minutes, then move to the next exercise. The clock keeps you honest.

3️⃣ Finish with THE LADDER: 1 rep, rest, 2 reps, rest, 3 reps... climb until you can't complete a round. Log your total reps — that's your score to beat next week.

📅 Your week: Lift Mon · Tue · Thu · Fri. Optional 30-min conditioning Wed + Sat.

Every exercise tells you exactly what to do. Follow the app, add weight each week, and watch your numbers climb. Glad you're here. 🤝
